data.executive_summary:
# Executive Summary

Ausecurity delivers expert GRC consulting and penetration testing services to businesses across Australia. This report covers an authorized security assessment of the public website. Testing was performed on 5 October 2026 with the owner’s permission and was limited to **ausecurity.best**.

## Overall result

The assessment confirmed **8 findings**: **1 high**, **4 medium**, **2 low**, and **1 informational**.

This report keeps the CVSS vectors from the verified findings file. Two items labelled low in that file (the HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect on `/api`, and missing SPF/DMARC) score as medium under CVSS 3.1. The chart therefore shows 1 high, 6 medium, and 1 informational.

The most serious issue is that the admin dashboard is reachable without logging in. It includes client-looking contact details and internal business figures. The site only tries to hide this with JavaScript after the page is already sent.

A “thank you” page can run script from the address bar (cross-site scripting). The login page can send users to an attacker site after sign-in. HTTPS uses a self-signed certificate, and standard browser-protection headers are missing.

Lower-priority issues are an HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect on `/api`, no SPF or DMARC email-authentication records, and nginx version disclosure.

## Highest-priority actions

1. Take the dashboard off the public internet until server-side login is required.
2. Fix the thank-you page to use text, not HTML.
3. Install a trusted certificate.
4. Add security headers.

data.scope:
This assessment covered only the owner-approved public website. Testing was performed on 5 October 2026 after authorization was confirmed via a required response header on the main public-facing website. The header value is not recorded in this report.

**In-scope (owner approved)**

| System | Description |
|:---|:---|
| https://ausecurity.best/ | Official public website and same-origin paths on ausecurity.best |

**Enumerated hosts (inventory only — not tested)**

The owner explicitly did not approve the following for testing:

* www.ausecurity.best (51.79.166.148)
* contact.ausecurity.best (51.79.166.148)
* blog.ausecurity.best (51.79.167.208) — WordPress observed during enumeration only
* ticket.ausecurity.best (51.79.166.209) — osTicket installer observed during enumeration only
* 51.79.166.148 as a general host (unrelated services)

The official website resolves to 51.79.166.148. That address was used only for connectivity to the approved website.

**Rejected lookalikes (out of scope)**

* ausecurity.com.au
* ausecurity.com
* ausecurity.net

**Third-party exclusions (not tested)**

OVH AS16276, Spaceship DNS, Google Fonts, Google Maps, and Flinders email infrastructure.

**Allowed methods**

Authorization check, passive and active enumeration, TLS review, HTTP header review, path discovery, JavaScript and HTML review, unauthenticated access-control checks, a single invalid-login response-shape test, contact-form input tests, and a DNS mail-record check.

**Forbidden methods**

Brute force, password spraying, denial of service, social engineering, malware, and destructive tests. No exploitation beyond minimum proof.
data.provided_users: No user accounts were provided. Testing was unauthenticated only. Cookie security flags were not observed because no authenticated session was obtained.

appendix_sections.title: Methodology
appendix_sections.content:
The assessment followed a phased, non-destructive methodology:

1. Authorization check on the main public-facing website before any testing.
2. Passive and active enumeration of company-related assets.
3. Owner confirmation that only https://ausecurity.best/ and same-origin paths were in scope.
4. TLS review of the approved host.
5. HTTP security-header review.
6. Path discovery on the approved host (common wordlist).
7. JavaScript and HTML review of public pages.
8. Unauthenticated access-control checks on the dashboard and related endpoints.
9. A single invalid-login response-shape test.
10. Contact-form input tests.
11. DNS mail-record check for ausecurity.best.

No brute force, password spraying, denial of service, social engineering, malware, or destructive tests were used. Testing stopped at minimum proof.

appendix_sections.title: Limitations
appendix_sections.content:
The following limitations apply to this assessment:

* Other enumerated hosts (www, contact, blog, ticket, and the related IP addresses as general hosts) were not tested because the owner selected only the main website.
* No authenticated session was obtained, so cookie flags were not observed.
* Dashboard client records were not independently verified as production versus demo data. They were still served without authentication.
* Possible unsafe handling of contact field `h` (HTTP 500 when pointing at localhost) was not confirmed as server-side request forgery and is not reported as a finding.
* Testing was performed from a single vantage point on a single day (5 October 2026).
* Third-party infrastructure (OVH AS16276, Spaceship DNS, Google Fonts, Google Maps, Flinders email) was excluded.

appendix_sections.title: Coverage
appendix_sections.content:
Approved host coverage on ausecurity.best:

* Public website over HTTPS, including same-origin paths
* TLS certificate review
* HTTP security headers
* Unauthenticated dashboard access (`/dashboard`, `/dashboard.html`)
* Login page and client-side redirect handling
* Consultation success page and contact form (`/api/contact`)
* `/api` slash-redirect behaviour
* DNS records relevant to email authentication (SPF, DMARC, MX, TXT, CAA)
* Server header disclosure

Enumerated but not tested: www.ausecurity.best, contact.ausecurity.best, blog.ausecurity.best, ticket.ausecurity.best, and IP addresses as general hosts.
